Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman identifies AI funding and agent-enabled financial disintermediation as growing risks, reviews mostly resilient bank credit and explicitly abandons his old banks-as-leading-indicator rule. His bank valuation logic is coherent, but AI contagion and next-recession claims exceed the verified evidence.

Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.

### 009. If agents move idle deposits to higher-yield instruments and banks must retain funding at higher rates, bank and brokerage net interest margins fall.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 8:13-9:55](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-market-cracks-under-ai-debt-burdenthe) | Stance: conditional | Horizon: not stated

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning: Net interest income equals interest on assets minus interest on funding. Raising the funding rate on a positive balance reduces net interest income and margin, all else equal.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

### 022. Higher sustainable returns on tangible equity justify higher price-to-tangible-book valuations when risk, growth and accounting are otherwise comparable.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

## Framework and tools

- Separate current loan quality from forward stock valuation.
- Decompose bank revenue and distinguish GAAP from settlement-adjusted returns.
- Use sustainable ROTCE relative to required returns to interpret tangible-book multiples.
- Monitor funding dependence and agent-driven erosion of customer inertia.
- Explicitly revises the banks-as-economy-leading-indicator rule.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- JPMorgan and BofA nonaccrual comparisons
- Bank EPS and ROTCE comparison
- Bank price-to-tangible-book ranges
- CoreWeave debt, leases and secondary bond yield
- Telecom year-to-date performance and P/E comparison
